title: College Algebra & Trigonometry
introduction: Prepare a learner to manipulate mathematical models, interpret graphs, solve constrained problems, and enter calculus, introductory physics, and programming with dependable algebra and trigonometry skills.

lessons.title: Linear equations and formula rearrangement
lessons.objective: Isolate a specified variable, state any divisor restrictions, and verify a proposed solution by substitution.

lessons.title: Inequalities and absolute value
lessons.objective: Express the full solution set of a linear, compound, or absolute-value inequality with correct endpoints.

lessons.title: Quadratics and complex roots
lessons.objective: Choose a quadratic solution method, return every root in the requested number system, and verify the roots.

lessons.title: Restrictions and extraneous solutions
lessons.objective: Solve rational and radical equations while preserving original restrictions and rejecting invalid candidate roots.

lessons.title: Function notation, domains, and piecewise rules
lessons.objective: Determine whether a relation is a function, evaluate it correctly, and describe its domain and range.

lessons.title: Transformations and graph features
lessons.objective: Predict how a transformation changes key points, intercepts, domain, and range.

lessons.title: Composition and inverse functions
lessons.objective: Compose functions with valid input restrictions and determine whether a domain restriction is needed for an inverse.

lessons.title: Rates of change and linear calibration
lessons.objective: Construct a linear model from two points, interpret its parameters with units, and judge the validity of a prediction.

lessons.title: Degree and end behavior
lessons.objective: Predict a polynomial's end behavior and possible number of turning points from its leading term.

lessons.title: Zeros, multiplicity, and graph shape
lessons.objective: Read zeros and multiplicities from factored form and explain crossing or touching behavior.

lessons.title: Division, remainders, and factors
lessons.objective: Divide a polynomial, state quotient and remainder, and use the remainder to test a proposed factor.

lessons.title: Finding and checking all polynomial roots
lessons.objective: Use rational-root candidates and factor reduction to obtain a complete root list, including multiplicities and complex pairs when requested.

lessons.title: Holes, asymptotes, and intercepts
lessons.objective: Identify original domain exclusions, removable holes, vertical asymptotes, intercepts, and end behavior of a rational function.

lessons.title: Polynomial and rational inequalities
lessons.objective: Build a sign chart and return every interval satisfying a polynomial or rational inequality.

lessons.title: Variation and rational models
lessons.objective: Build a direct, inverse, or joint variation model and use units and restrictions to interpret a result.

lessons.title: Radical functions and restricted inverses
lessons.objective: Analyze a radical function's domain and range and verify an inverse on the correct restricted domain.

lessons.title: Exponential functions and growth factors
lessons.objective: Distinguish additive from multiplicative change and interpret an exponential model's initial value, base, and asymptote.

lessons.title: Logarithms as inverse functions
lessons.objective: Convert between exponential and logarithmic statements and determine the domain of a logarithmic expression.

lessons.title: Log rules and exponential equations
lessons.objective: Apply logarithm rules with valid domains and solve exponential or logarithmic equations with complete solution checks.

lessons.title: Decay, thresholds, and logarithmic scales
lessons.objective: Fit a simple exponential model, solve for a threshold time, and interpret a logarithm of a dimensionless ratio.

lessons.title: Radians, rotations, and arc length
lessons.objective: Convert degree and radian measures, identify coterminal angles, and calculate an arc length with consistent units.

lessons.title: Right-triangle ratios
lessons.objective: Choose a trigonometric ratio to solve a right triangle and interpret the solution with the correct reference angle and units.

lessons.title: The unit circle and exact values
lessons.objective: Determine exact sine and cosine values using coordinates, symmetry, reference angles, and quadrant signs.

lessons.title: All six trigonometric functions
lessons.objective: Calculate the six trigonometric ratios where defined and explain each undefined value using a zero denominator.

lessons.title: Sine and cosine parameters
lessons.objective: Determine amplitude, period, midline, and phase shift and construct a matching sinusoidal function.

lessons.title: Tangent and reciprocal graphs
lessons.objective: Predict periods, asymptotes, and domains of transformed tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions.

lessons.title: Inverse trigonometric functions and principal values
lessons.objective: Evaluate arcsine, arccosine, and arctangent within their principal ranges and distinguish them from solving a periodic equation.

lessons.title: Signals, frequency, and time shifts
lessons.objective: Fit a simple periodic signal from extrema and timing information and interpret frequency and phase in consistent units.

lessons.title: Identities and domain-aware simplification
lessons.objective: Verify an identity through valid transformations on its common domain and identify invalid proof steps.

lessons.title: Angle sums and double angles
lessons.objective: Use sum, difference, and double-angle identities to evaluate exact expressions and explain invalid distributive shortcuts.

lessons.title: Complete trigonometric solution sets
lessons.objective: Find every solution on a stated interval and express general periodic families when requested.

lessons.title: Non-right triangles and model ambiguity
lessons.objective: Choose the law of sines or cosines, solve a non-right triangle, and identify whether supplied measurements permit zero, one, or two triangles.

lessons.title: Two-variable linear systems
lessons.objective: Solve a two-variable system and distinguish one solution, no solution, and infinitely many solutions.

lessons.title: Three-variable elimination
lessons.objective: Reduce a three-variable system to simpler equations and verify the resulting ordered triple or describe a dependent family.

lessons.title: Nonlinear intersections and feasible regions
lessons.objective: Find all solutions of a small nonlinear system and interpret whether points satisfy simultaneous inequalities.

lessons.title: Formulating and auditing systems
lessons.objective: Define variables and units, translate two or three supplied relationships into a system, and assess whether its solution is meaningful.

lessons.title: Matrix dimensions and operations
lessons.objective: Determine whether matrix operations are defined and compute sums, scalar products, and matrix products correctly.

lessons.title: Augmented matrices and row reduction
lessons.objective: Represent a linear system as an augmented matrix and use valid row operations to classify and solve it.

lessons.title: Determinants and inverse matrices
lessons.objective: Use a 2x2 determinant to decide invertibility, compute an inverse when it exists, and solve a system by multiplication in the correct order.

lessons.title: Choosing methods and checking numerical results
lessons.objective: Select an appropriate system solution method, use Cramer's rule for a small nonsingular case, and verify a rounded result using residuals.

bridges.title: Signed numbers, fractions, and notation
bridges.objective: Compute with signed fractions; distinguish a negative base from a leading minus; interpret interval endpoints and exact versus approximate answers.

bridges.title: Powers, roots, and scientific notation
bridges.objective: Integer and rational exponents, scientific notation, even-root domains, and the distinction between sqrt(x^2) and x.

bridges.title: Expansion and factoring
bridges.objective: Distribute with signs, collect like terms, factor common factors and simple quadratics, and check by expansion.

bridges.title: Fractions containing variables
bridges.objective: Find common denominators, cancel factors only, state original exclusions, and divide rational expressions without dividing by zero.

bridges.title: Coordinates, lines, and measurement labels
bridges.objective: Read coordinates and scales, calculate rise over run, distinguish vertical and horizontal lines, and keep units attached to modeled quantities.

bridges.title: Right triangles and calculator use
bridges.objective: Use the Pythagorean relation, identify the side opposite an angle, enter parentheses correctly, and check degree versus radian mode.
